heroHeadline: Carney Courts EU as Canada's First Associate Member; Trump Calls It a 'Hostile Act' as Mexico Reports 'Very Good' Tariff Call
heroSubtitle: PM Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Sept 17, telling MEPs 'we are not fair-weather allies,' after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed Canada become the EU's first associate member under an 'Alliance for the Future' beyond the existing CETA deal. Trump called the potential partnership a possible 'hostile act,' branded Canada a 'terrible trade partner,' and threatened 'very heavy tariffs on Europe'; Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre accused Carney of inconsistency. No new US-Canada bilateral session has been confirmed since the Aug 21 collapse. Separately, President Sheinbaum said her 22nd call with Trump on Sept 16 was 'very good,' with 'some agreements' reached though no terms disclosed; Mexico is still seeking relief from 50% steel/aluminum and auto tariffs, and the fourth USMCA bilateral round is now confirmed for Sept 28-29 in Washington, with both governments reportedly racing to close a deal before the Nov 3 US midterms. Canada's TSX closed the week at 35,806.65 (-0.19%) after a volatile stretch; the peso strengthened to 17.15/USD following the Fed's Sept 16 rate hike. Sept 8 US-Canada tariffs and import bans remain in effect.
